newsitem.title: USA: NBA basketball-CARLESIMO NAMED NEW COACH OF GOLDEN STATE WARRIORS.
newsitem.headline: NBA basketball-CARLESIMO NAMED NEW COACH OF GOLDEN STATE WARRIORS.

text.p: P.J. Carlesimo, recently dismissed as coach of the Portland Trail Blazers, on Thursday was named head coach of the Golden State Warriors.
Carlesimo signed a five-year contract with Golden State. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The 48-year-old Carlesimo was fired last month by Portland, ending a three-year stint with the team. The Trail Blazers finished 49-33 this past season, but were eliminated in the first round of the playoffs for the third successive year under Carlesimo.
"This is a great franchise with a rich tradition and the challenge of building upon that tradition excites me," said Carlesimo at a news conference.

Carlesimo coached at Seton Hall for 12 seasons and took the Pirates to the 1989 NCAA Championship game. He accepted the head coaching position with Portland in 1994 and compiled a 137-109 record in three years.

"P.J. Carlesimo is the right fit for our organisation," said Warriors owner Christopher Cohan. "He has enjoyed success on every level, and he has done a remarkable job in his first three seasons in the NBA."

Carlesimo served as an assistant on Chuck Daly's staff for the 1992 United States Olympic "Dream Team," which won the gold medal in Barcelona. Current Warrior Chris Mullin was an original member of the squad.

The hiring of Carlesimo marks the second consecutive time the Warriors turned to a former Blazers coach to fill their coaching vacancy. Rick Adelman spent six seasons as coach of the Trail Blazers before joining Golden State in 1995.
Al Attles will remain as the team's acting general manager, but Carlesimo said the search has begun for a permanent general manager.
